text.en: The poem has the frog describe how it lives, hides and moves.

The frog sits in ponds and in the rain, and also hops about in muddy drains.
As a tadpole it swims as a tiny, clear fish-like creature.
It flicks its tongue to catch food very fast, and it lives on land and in water, in damp places.
Its colours match plants and trees, so it hides well in grass and leaves, but it must beware of snakes.
It croaks loudly, feels proud of its pond, jumps high and swims easily with webbed feet.
The theme is the frog's way of life and how it is suited to its surroundings.
(additional, not in the textbook) Frogs live both in water and on land, so they are called amphibians.
